prompt.context: Our client is a large national retailer whose music segment has seen declining profits over the last couple of years. You have been hired to help deal with this problem.
prompt.question: Why have profits declined, and what should the client do to address it?

clarifying_info.a: Profits used to be $80M but are currently very low.

clarifying_info.q: What does the supply chain look like?
clarifying_info.a: Suppliers sell directly to us. No logistics costs.
There are 4 big players in the market all similar size to us. We do not know if they are making money. Two are similar large retailers and two are specialized music suppliers.
The market has been shrinking over the last couple of years.
We hold both new releases and catalog CDs.

clarifying_info.q: Can you share the income statement?
clarifying_info.a: Revenues from New CDs: $704M; Revenues from Catalogs: $444M; Total COGS: $900M; Store rental overhead: $150M; Labor expense: $90M; Profit: $8M.

clarifying_info.q: What are the prices and costs per CD?
clarifying_info.a: The price of a new CD is $12 and the price of a catalog CD is $15. The cost to us of either type of CD is $10 and is similar to other players' cost. We hold minimal inventory.
90% of our space is catalogs and 10% is used for new CDs.

framework: Diagnose the profit decline: decompose into revenue and cost drivers
Segment the P&L by product line (new CDs vs. catalog CDs) using Activity Based Costing
Allocate overhead (space and labor) proportionally to each segment
Determine which segment is profitable and which is not
Assess strategic options: optimize space allocation, evaluate cross-selling risk, identify alternative uses for freed space

questions.prompt: Using Activity Based Costing, allocate revenues, COGS, space overhead, and labor to new CDs vs. catalog CDs and determine per-segment profitability.
questions.guidance: Candidate should recognize that space overhead ($150M) should be allocated 10%/90% (new/catalog) and labor ($90M) proportionally to volume. Volume is derived from revenues divided by price. Key insight: catalog CDs have much lower margin per unit ($5 vs. $2 for new) but consume 90% of space, making them unprofitable on a fully-loaded basis.

math.setup: New CD price = $12, Catalog CD price = $15, cost of either = $10. New CD revenues = $704M, Catalog revenues = $444M. Space: 10% new / 90% catalog. Labor allocated by volume share.
steps: Volume of new CDs: $704M / $12 = ~58.7M units (casebook rounds to ~60M)
Volume of catalog CDs: $444M / $15 = ~29.6M units (casebook rounds to ~30M)
COGS new: 60M x $10 = $600M; COGS catalog: 30M x $10 = $300M
Space overhead new: 10% x $150M = $15M; catalog: 90% x $150M = $135M
math.answer: New CD segment is profitable (~$30M profit); Catalog CD segment is loss-making (~-$20M loss). Total = ~$8M, matching the income statement.

brainstorming.prompt: What should the client do with the space currently occupied by catalog CDs?

categories.name: Optimize catalog operations
ideas: Reduce catalog SKUs to top-sellers only
Shift catalog to online/on-demand to eliminate physical shelf space
Negotiate better terms with catalog suppliers to improve margins

categories.name: Reduce or eliminate catalog
ideas: Phase out catalog CDs gradually to test revenue impact
Assess cross-selling: do catalog browsers also buy new releases?
Analyze customer traffic driven by catalog selection

categories.name: Repurpose freed space
ideas: Add adjacent categories: DVDs, video games, accessories
Convert to an experience/listening zone to drive traffic

recommendation: The low profitability is driven by the catalog CD business, which loses approximately $20M annually when overhead is fully allocated on a space basis
The new CD business remains profitable at approximately $30M
risks: Removing catalog CDs may reduce store traffic and hurt new CD cross-sales
Market for new CDs is also shrinking, so the underlying trend needs monitoring
Competitors may react if we cede catalog space
next_steps: Quantify cross-selling dependency: how much new CD revenue is driven by catalog browsers
Identify the best alternative use for the 90% of space currently held by catalogs
Evaluate whether a reduced catalog footprint (top-selling titles only) could restore profitability without sacrificing traffic
